slides.title: Festivals Are Joy Days 🎉
slides.text: A festival is a special day of joy! We wear new clothes, make tasty food, decorate our homes and celebrate with family, friends and neighbours.
slides.spoken: Festivals are special days of joy that we share together.

slides.title: National Festivals 🇮🇳
slides.text: The WHOLE of India celebrates national festivals together! Independence Day on 15 August, Republic Day on 26 January, and Gandhi Jayanti on 2 October.
slides.spoken: Independence Day, Republic Day and Gandhi Jayanti are national festivals.

slides.title: Festivals of Light, Colour and Prayer 🪔
slides.text: Diwali is the festival of LIGHTS with lamps and rangoli. Holi splashes COLOURS of spring. Eid brings sewaiyan and moon-sighting. Christmas glows with stars and carols. Every festival is beautiful!
slides.spoken: Diwali, Holi, Eid and Christmas are celebrated with lights, colours, food and prayers.

slides.title: Harvest Festivals 🌾
slides.text: Farmers celebrate when crops are ready! PONGAL in Tamil Nadu, BAISAKHI in Punjab, ONAM in Kerala — they thank nature for the harvest with feasts and dances.
slides.spoken: Pongal, Baisakhi and Onam thank nature for a good harvest.

slides.title: We Celebrate Together 🤗
slides.text: The best part of festivals? Sharing! Give sweets to neighbours, enjoy your friends' festivals too, and respect every celebration. Together is the way of India!
slides.spoken: Sharing sweets and respecting all festivals brings us together.

challenges.question: Which one is a NATIONAL festival of India?
challenges.hint: National festivals belong to the whole country!
challenges.misconception: Independence Day is celebrated by the whole nation.

challenges.question: When do we celebrate Independence Day?
challenges.hint: The day India became free — mid-August!
challenges.misconception: India celebrates Independence Day on 15 August.

challenges.question: Which festival is called the festival of LIGHTS?
challenges.hint: Lamps, diyas and rangoli glow everywhere!
challenges.misconception: Diwali is the festival of lights.

challenges.question: Which festival is full of COLOURS?
challenges.hint: People splash gulal and colours on friends!
challenges.misconception: Holi is the festival of colours.

challenges.question: Pongal and Baisakhi are ______ festivals.
challenges.hint: Farmers thank nature when crops are ready!
challenges.misconception: Pongal and Baisakhi are harvest festivals.

challenges.question: Sort each festival: national festival or other festival?
challenges.hint: National festivals are celebrated by the whole country.
challenges.misconception: Republic Day and Gandhi Jayanti are national. Diwali and Christmas are other festivals.

challenges.question: How should we enjoy festivals?
options: Only my festival is the best
challenges.hint: Think of the happiest, kindest way to celebrate!
challenges.misconception: Sharing sweets and enjoying every festival together is the best way.

challenges.question: Gandhi Jayanti is the birthday of which great leader?
challenges.hint: The father of our nation — born on 2 October!
challenges.misconception: Gandhi Jayanti celebrates Mahatma Gandhi's birthday on 2 October.
